title: Flat extension of an invertible ordinary base-tensor comparison
statement: For commutative R-algebras A and B, an arbitrary complex Q of A-modules, an E=A tensor_R B algebra D flat over E, and any BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B Q D [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model], assume comparison i is invertible for every i. Then localizedComparison i is invertible for every i. There is no boundedness, projectivity, Tor-independence or localization hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change: local affine reduction and Tor-independent comparison of derived tensors

proof.text: Let f be A → E and g be E → D. Transfer hflat to D with the restricted E-action using Module.ext and Algebra.smul_def. Apply Module.Flat.lTensor_exact to every exact short complex and Functor.exact_tfae to obtain PreservesFiniteLimits for extension along g. Its adjunction supplies preservation of finite colimits. No same-ring-universe descent theorem is used.

Construct the scalar-extension composition isomorphism c directly by conjugateIsoEquiv from restrictScalarsComp and the composite extension/restriction adjunction. unit_conjugateEquiv_symm identifies its hom on 1 tensor q with 1 tensor (1 tensor q). Map c.symm to complexes to obtain e: g-extension of K ≅ T. ExtendScalars.hom_ext and ordinaryToLocalized_tmul show that ordinaryToLocalized in each degree is exactly the adjoint of e.hom. This is the mixed-universe version of Mathlib extendScalarsComp and needs no new deferred theorem.

For S=K.sc i and U=T.sc i, let ψ be the short-complex map induced by e.hom, h and k their left homology data, and γ the homology map data from h.map F to k. ψ is invertible, so γ.quasiIso_iff gives IsIso γ.φH. Transpose γ.φK and γ.φH through the adjunction to define homology map data δ for ordinaryToLocalized into U.map G. The three data equations follow from homEquiv_naturality_left/right, the termwise transpose equality, and the three equations of γ. δ.homologyMap_eq and k.mapHomologyIso_eq identify the cohomology adjunct with F.map h.homologyIso.hom, then γ.φH, then k.homologyIso.inv; all are invertible.

Use injectivity of the adjunction homEquiv and its left naturality with M.localized_eq to identify M.localizedComparison i with F.map (M.comparison i) followed by the preceding cohomology adjunct. The assumed comparison is invertible and functors preserve isomorphisms. Both factors are therefore invertible.
